questions.title: What do you do if your ball stops on the wrong green?
questions.question: If your ball lands on a green that isn't the hole you are playing, what should you do?

choices.text: Hit your shot from the wrong green
Pick up your ball and drop it off the wrong green for free
Move your ball and add one extra shot
Ask another player what to do

questions.explanation: If your ball stops on the wrong green, you must pick it up and drop it off the green nearby without any extra shots. You cannot hit from the wrong green.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The smooth, short grass area with the hole on it where you putt your ball.
Letting the ball fall from knee height to put it back in play.

questions.teachingTip: Remind children that greens are special and must be protected, so you never hit shots off a green that isn't your own hole.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think they can play from any green.
Some might think they always get a penalty for moving their ball.

questions.title: What should you do if your ball lands on the wrong green?
questions.question: If your ball comes to rest on a putting green for a different hole than the one you’re playing, what are you required to do?

choices.text: Play your shot from the wrong green
Take a free drop off the wrong green
Move your ball with a one shot penalty

questions.explanation: If your ball is on a wrong green, you must take free relief and drop off the green; you are not allowed to play the ball from the wrong green.
